author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Use save states safely without replacing in-game saves
summary: Treat save states as version-sensitive checkpoints, keep memory-card saves authoritative, avoid cross-profile timeline conflicts, and recover cleanly when a state no longer loads.
heroAlt: EmuCoreX save manager with multiple game-specific state slots

blocks.text: A state freezes the emulator, not just the game

A save state captures CPU, memory, devices and renderer-related state at one instant. It can depend on core implementation and active settings, while an in-game save written to a PS2 memory card follows the console's normal persistence path. Loading an old state can also restore an earlier view of card-related state, creating confusing timeline conflicts.
Make an in-game memory-card save before relying on a state and again after important progress. Never keep the only copy of progress in a single quick-state slot.

Confirm the memory card is healthy and backed up. Note the active core/app version and per-game profile before creating long-lived checkpoints. Use named or rotating slots for milestones; reserve quick save/load for short-session recovery.

items: Verified in-game save on the active card.
Cold backup of the card before risky state work.
Known app/core version.
Two or more rotating state slots.
Stable per-game settings during create/load tests.

blocks.text: Create checkpoints with a durable escape route

items: 1. Save normally inside the game and wait until its write indicator or save screen has finished.
2. Create a state in a named slot, record the location or milestone, then continue playing.
3. Use another slot for the next milestone instead of overwriting the only known-good checkpoint.
4. Before updating the app/core or changing major CPU settings, make a fresh in-game save and cold-back up the memory card.
5. After the change, cold-boot the game and verify the in-game save first; load an old state only as an optional compatibility test.

blocks.text: A state passes when it loads twice under the same configuration, controls and audio resume, and a subsequent normal in-game save survives a cold boot. Also verify the older rotating slot. A thumbnail is not proof that the serialized state can be restored.

items: Corresponding in-game save exists.
State loads twice without renderer/audio/input faults.
Memory-card progress survives a cold boot.
At least one earlier state remains untouched.
Version and profile changes are documented.

blocks.text: If a state crashes or hangs, stop retrying after confirming the failure and cold-boot from the memory-card save. Restore the previous profile only when the state was created under it and doing so is safe. Never replace a newer memory card with an older one merely to satisfy a stale state without first backing up both timelines.

items: Cold-boot and load the in-game save.
Try the previous rotating state once under its recorded profile.
Back up both current and historical card files before reconciling progress.
Delete a broken state only after durable progress is confirmed.
State thumbnail exists but load fails: serialization/core compatibility changed.
Game loads with old progress: state restored an earlier timeline.
State works only with old hacks: profile dependency was not recorded.
Quick slot overwritten: no rotation or named milestone existed.

blocks.text: The safest hierarchy is simple: in-game save, cold memory-card backup, then rotating save states. States make play convenient; cards make progress portable and recoverable. Use each for the job it can reliably perform.
